title: Indefinite adjectives (chaque, quelque, tout…)
summary: chaque (each, every) never changes and is followed by a singular noun with no article: chaque matin, chaque fille.
quelques (a few, some) is plural and goes before the noun: quelques amis, quelques idées.
plusieurs (several) never changes and is always plural: plusieurs fois, plusieurs villes.
tout agrees with the noun and is followed by the article: tout le temps, toute la journée, tous les jours, toutes les semaines.
tous les / toutes les + time word = every: tous les samedis = chaque samedi.
autre agrees in number; des becomes d' in front of it: un autre jour, d'autres pays.
même before a noun means same and agrees in number: la même école, les mêmes vêtements.
certains / certaines (some, certain) agree with a plural noun: certains profs, certaines matières.
tout le monde means everyone and takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là.

cards.front: What does chaque mean, and does it ever change form?
cards.back: chaque = each / every. It never changes and is always followed by a singular noun with no article: chaque jour, chaque semaine, chaque élève.

cards.front: Give the four forms of tout + the definite article.
cards.back: tout le (masc. sing.), toute la (fem. sing.), tous les (masc. plural), toutes les (fem. plural): tout le week-end, toute la classe, tous les garçons, toutes les filles.

cards.why: journée is feminine singular, so tout becomes toute.

cards.prompt: Nous avons cours de français ___ les jours.
cards.en: We have French lessons every day.
cards.why: jours is masculine plural, so tout becomes tous; tous les jours = every day.

cards.prompt: Dans ma classe, ___ les filles aiment la natation.
cards.en: In my class, all the girls like swimming.
cards.why: filles is feminine plural, so tout becomes toutes.

cards.prompt: Mon petit frère a mangé ___ le gâteau !
cards.en: My little brother ate the whole cake!
cards.why: gâteau is masculine singular, so tout stays as it is: tout le gâteau = the whole cake.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using chaque instead of the words in bold.
cards.prompt: Je fais du sport **tous les matins**.
answers: Je fais du sport chaque matin.
Chaque matin, je fais du sport.
cards.why: chaque is followed by a singular noun with no article: tous les matins = chaque matin.

cards.front: quelques or plusieurs: what is the difference?
cards.back: quelques = a few / some (a small number): quelques minutes. plusieurs = several (more than one; it never changes): plusieurs semaines. Both go before a plural noun with no article.

cards.prompt: J'ai acheté ___ cartes postales pour mes grands-parents.
cards.en: I bought a few postcards for my grandparents.
cards.why: Before a plural noun quelque takes an -s: quelques cartes = a few cards.

cards.prompt: Nous sommes allés à Paris ___ fois.
cards.en: We have been to Paris several times.
cards.why: plusieurs (several) is always plural and never changes form.

cards.front: Why do you say d'autres pays and not des autres pays for 'other countries'?
cards.back: When an adjective comes before a plural noun, des becomes de (d' before a vowel): d'autres pays, d'autres idées. Singular: un autre jour, une autre fois.

cards.prompt: L'année prochaine, je voudrais visiter d'___ pays.
cards.en: Next year I would like to visit other countries.
cards.why: autre agrees in number with the plural noun pays, so it adds -s; des becomes d' before it.

cards.instruction: Make the words in bold plural.
cards.why: The plural of un is normally des, but des becomes d' before the adjective autres; autre and stylo both add -s.

cards.front: What does même mean before a noun, and how does it agree?
cards.back: Before a noun même = same. It agrees in number only (no feminine change, as it already ends in -e): le même prof, la même équipe, les mêmes idées.

cards.prompt: Mes amis et moi portons les ___ baskets.
cards.en: My friends and I wear the same trainers.
cards.why: même agrees in number with the plural noun baskets, so it adds -s: les mêmes baskets.

cards.prompt: Pour moi, ___ matières sont plus faciles que d'autres.
cards.en: For me, some subjects are easier than others.
cards.why: certain agrees with matières, which is feminine plural: certaines.

cards.front: What does tout le monde mean, and is the verb singular or plural?
cards.back: tout le monde = everyone / everybody. It takes a singular verb: Tout le monde est content. Tout le monde aime les vacances.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using the correct form of tout + les instead of chaque. Change the verb too.
answers: Toutes les maisons ont un jardin.
cards.en: All the houses have a garden.
cards.why: maison is feminine, so chaque maison becomes toutes les maisons; the subject is now plural, so a becomes ont.
